## Load packages

`GO.db`, `AnnotationDbi`, `eulerr` and `enrichVolcano` (the user's own package, not on CRAN) are
called with `::` for one job each.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, patchwork, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/07_leading_edge/a_script/07_leading_edge.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

The question: for pathways both legs move the same way with training, do the same proteins drive
them? The comparison uses fgsea leading edges. In gene set enrichment, proteins are ranked by
their training statistic and a running sum walks down the ranking, rising at each set member; the
leading edge is the set members ranked before the running sum peaks, the ones carrying the
enrichment. This step reads the fgsea run `01_run_fgsea_and_fry` already made, so nothing is
re-ranked. Adapted from Sam's PR #26 (sc-norton).

Three inputs: the `set_tests` sheet from `01_run_fgsea_and_fry` (one row per set, method and
contrast, leading edges as `;`-joined symbols), the set catalogue and the gene sets themselves
from `00_build_gene_sets`.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "07_leading_edge")
set_tests <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry", "c_data", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx"),
  "set_tests"
)
set_catalog <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"),
  "set_catalog"
)
sets <- readRDS(here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "gene_sets.rds"))
arms <- c(BFR = "BFR_Post-Pre", HLRT = "HLRT_Post-Pre")
arm_colours <- c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC")
dim(set_tests)
```

## Select the shared pathways

Keep the fgsea rows for the two training contrasts, one per leg. A pathway is kept when fgsea
calls it at FDR < 0.05 in both legs, with the same sign of NES (normalised enrichment score, the
direction and strength of the enrichment), and when it is a main set after `collapsePathways` in
at least one leg, so one representative stands for each cluster of overlapping sets.

```{r shared-sets}
fgsea <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% arms) |>
  mutate(arm = names(arms)[match(contrast, arms)]) |>
  select(set_id, database, pathway, arm, NES, padj, main, leadingEdge)
shared_sets <- fgsea |>
  summarise(
    keep = all(padj < 0.05) && n_distinct(sign(NES)) == 1 && any(main), .by = set_id
  ) |>
  filter(keep) |>
  pull(set_id)
length(shared_sets)
```

## Compare the leading edges

Split each kept pathway's leading edges into one row per protein, then record which legs list
that protein: BFR only, HLRT only or both.

```{r proteins}
proteins <- fgsea |>
  filter(set_id %in% shared_sets) |>
  separate_longer_delim(leadingEdge, ";") |>
  rename(gene = leadingEdge) |>
  summarise(
    in_arm = paste(sort(arm), collapse = " and "), .by = c(set_id, database, pathway, gene)
  ) |>
  mutate(in_arm = recode(in_arm, "BFR and HLRT" = "both"))
head(proteins, 4)
```

Count the three groups per pathway and add the Jaccard index: proteins in both leading edges over
proteins in either. It reads 1 when the legs share every driver and 0 when they share none. Each
leg's NES rides along, and rows sort from the lowest overlap.

```{r leading-edge}
leading_edge <- proteins |>
  count(set_id, database, pathway, in_arm) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = in_arm, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(jaccard = both / (both + BFR + HLRT)) |>
  left_join(
    fgsea |>
      select(set_id, arm, NES) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = NES, names_prefix = "NES_"),
    by = "set_id"
  ) |>
  arrange(jaccard) |>
  mutate(label = enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 1000))
head(select(leading_edge, label, both, BFR, HLRT, jaccard), 6)
```

Leading edges shift with small changes in the ranking, so this overlap describes and does not
test.

## Break GO:BP parents into children

For each GO:BP pathway both legs move, look up its direct child terms in the GO hierarchy
(`GO.db::GOBPCHILDREN`) and keep those that were tested as sets. `go_ids` maps set IDs to GO
identifiers; `mget()` returns each parent's children, `NA` where there are none.

```{r go-lookup}
go_ids <- set_catalog |>
  filter(database == "GOBP", qualifies) |>
  select(set_id, source_id)
parents <- inner_join(filter(leading_edge, database == "GOBP"), go_ids, by = "set_id")
go_children_of <- AnnotationDbi::mget(parents$source_id, GO.db::GOBPCHILDREN, ifnotfound = NA)
nrow(parents)
```

`by_arm` repeats each leading-edge protein once per leg that lists it. For every parent, child
and leg, `proteins` counts how many of the parent's leading-edge proteins in that leg belong to
the child term. Child terms overlap, so these are counts only, with no test across them.

```{r go-children}
by_arm <- proteins |>
  mutate(arm = if_else(in_arm == "both", "BFR;HLRT", in_arm)) |>
  separate_longer_delim(arm, ";")
go_children <- parents |>
  transmute(parent_id = set_id, parent = label, child_go = map(source_id, function(id) {
    unname(go_children_of[[id]])
  })) |>
  unnest(child_go) |>
  inner_join(rename(go_ids, child_id = set_id, child_go = source_id), by = "child_go") |>
  mutate(child = enrichVolcano::clean_label(
    set_catalog$pathway[match(child_id, set_catalog$set_id)], width = 1000
  )) |>
  cross_join(tibble(arm = names(arms))) |>
  mutate(proteins = pmap_int(list(parent_id, child_id, arm), function(parent_id, child_id, arm) {
    sum(by_arm$gene[by_arm$set_id == parent_id & by_arm$arm == arm] %in% sets[[child_id]])
  }))
head(select(go_children, parent, child, arm, proteins), 6)
```

## Draw figures

All pages share a caption style, with captions wrapped at 115 characters.

```{r page-style}
page_theme <- theme(
  plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
  plot.caption.position = "plot"
)
```

S20 puts every shared pathway on one page: a bar per pathway split into proteins in both leading
edges and in one leg only, lowest overlap at the bottom of each collection.

```{r overlap-page}
overlap_page <- leading_edge |>
  mutate(label = factor(str_trunc(label, 60), unique(str_trunc(label, 60)))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(both, BFR, HLRT), names_to = "in_arm", values_to = "proteins") |>
  mutate(in_arm = factor(in_arm, c("BFR", "both", "HLRT"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(proteins, label, fill = in_arm)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  facet_grid(database ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(BFR = "#B2182B", both = "grey55", HLRT = "#2166AC"), name = "leading edge in"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "leading-edge proteins", y = NULL,
    caption = str_wrap(paste(
      "S20 Figure. Leading-edge overlap between the legs. Every pathway that fgsea calls at FDR",
      sprintf("< 0.05 in both training contrasts, in the same direction (%d,", nrow(leading_edge)),
      "each a main set after collapse in at least one leg). Bars split each pathway's",
      "leading-edge proteins into those shared by both legs and those in one leg only; lowest",
      "overlap at the bottom of each collection. Leading edges move with small ranking changes,",
      "so this describes and does not test. Data: leading_edge sheet of 07_leading_edge.xlsx."
    ), 115)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6), strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
    legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  page_theme
```

S21 is Sam's Venn view: one Venn diagram per pathway, circle areas proportional to the counts
(`eulerr` fits them), with the shared proteins named beneath, six to a page. `venn()` takes a set
ID and returns that pathway's panel. `euler()` starts its layout search from random positions, so
the seed keeps the drawing the same between renders.

```{r venn-pages}
set.seed(1)
venn <- function(id) {
  counts <- filter(leading_edge, set_id == id)
  fit <- eulerr::euler(c(BFR = counts$BFR, HLRT = counts$HLRT, "BFR&HLRT" = counts$both))
  shared <- sort(filter(proteins, set_id == id, in_arm == "both")$gene)
  wrap_elements(full = plot(
    fit,
    fills = list(fill = arm_colours, alpha = 0.6), quantities = list(fontsize = 8),
    labels = list(fontsize = 8)
  )) +
    labs(
      title = str_wrap(counts$label, 45), subtitle = str_wrap(paste(shared, collapse = " "), 70)
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 5, lineheight = 1.1)
    )
}
venn_pages <- split(leading_edge$set_id, ceiling(seq_along(leading_edge$set_id) / 6)) |>
  imap(function(ids, page) {
    wrap_plots(map(ids, venn), ncol = 2) +
      plot_annotation(caption = str_wrap(sprintf(paste(
        "S21 Figure (page %s of %d). Leading edges by leg, one Venn per pathway in the order of",
        "S20. Areas follow the counts of proteins in each leg's leading edge only and in both;",
        "the proteins shared by both legs are listed under each title. Data: proteins sheet of",
        "07_leading_edge.xlsx."
      ), page, ceiling(nrow(leading_edge) / 6)), 115), theme = page_theme)
  })
```

S22 draws the GO:BP parents with their child terms, eight parents to a page: BFR counts to the
left of zero, HLRT to the right.

```{r child-pages}
child_pages <- go_children |>
  mutate(
    proteins = if_else(arm == "BFR", -proteins, proteins),
    parent = str_wrap(parent, 45), child = str_trunc(child, 50),
    page = ceiling(match(parent, unique(parent)) / 8)
  ) |>
  split(~page) |>
  imap(function(rows, page) {
    ggplot(rows, aes(proteins, child, fill = arm)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.7) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
      facet_wrap(~parent, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = arm_colours, name = NULL) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = abs) +
      labs(
        x = "parent's leading-edge proteins in the child term (BFR left, HLRT right)", y = NULL,
        caption = str_wrap(sprintf(paste(
          "S22 Figure (page %s of %d). GO:BP pathways both legs move, broken into their tested",
          "child terms. Bars count the parent's leading-edge proteins in each child, BFR to the",
          "left and HLRT to the right. Child terms overlap, so the counts are not tested. Data:",
          "go_children sheet of 07_leading_edge.xlsx."
        ), page, ceiling(n_distinct(go_children$parent) / 8)), 115)
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
      theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(size = 6.5)) +
      page_theme
  })
```

All pages go to one A4 PDF, S20 first.

```{r write-figures}
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "07_leading_edge.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
walk(c(list(overlap_page), venn_pages, child_pages), print)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Summary

Shared pathways per collection, the spread of the Jaccard index, and the GO:BP breakdown: parents
with tested children, distinct child terms, parent and child pairs, and the pairs where one leg
holds at least five proteins and more than twice the other's count.

```{r summary}
count(leading_edge, database)
summary(leading_edge$jaccard)
slice_head(select(leading_edge, label, jaccard), n = 3)
c(
  parents = n_distinct(go_children$parent_id),
  children = n_distinct(go_children$child_id),
  pairs = nrow(distinct(go_children, parent_id, child_id))
)
go_children |>
  select(parent, child, arm, proteins) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = proteins) |>
  filter(pmax(BFR, HLRT) >= 5, pmax(BFR, HLRT) > 2 * pmin(BFR, HLRT))
```

## Save results

`07_leading_edge.xlsx` holds `leading_edge` (one row per pathway), `proteins` (one row per
pathway and leading-edge protein) and `go_children` (one row per parent, child and leg).

```{r write}
sheets <- list(leading_edge = leading_edge, proteins = proteins, go_children = go_children)
write_xlsx(sheets, file.path(stage, "c_data", "07_leading_edge.xlsx"))
```
